note: Golden .plur capsule fixtures, written by Python from §6 of the standard. §6 is STABLE and has no producer or consumer in the codebase, so these are the first bytes it has been asked to agree with. The negative cases are the point: §6.7 lists checks a reader MUST perform, and a check nobody has seen fail is not a check.

capsules.note: A well-formed v1 capsule with no flags set. Every §6.7 check passes.
§6.7 step 2: the first four bytes are not 50 4c 55 52. A reader MUST refuse rather than attempt to parse what follows.
§10.3 rule 3: a reader MUST reject an unknown FormatVersion rather than guess. This is what keeps the version space usable later.
§10.3 rule 4: reserved flag bits (2-15, mask 0xfffc) MUST be zero on write and MUST cause rejection on read. Accepting one now would make the bit unusable for its eventual meaning.
§6.7: the header's declared payload size does not match the bytes present.
§6.7 step 10 and §8: the recomputed payload hash does not match the header. A receiver MUST refuse to act on it.
§6.7 step 1: fewer than 12 bytes, so there is not even a preamble to read.
§6.7: the payload region underflows what the header declares.
§6.7 step 11: COMPRESSED is set but the header says compression:none. The flag and the descriptor MUST agree; a reader cannot know which to believe.

§6.8 step 4 and §7: SIGNED is set with no 64-byte trailer and signer:null. v1 producers MUST NOT set SIGNED at all, since the scheme is RESERVED — so a reader seeing it has an ambiguous envelope and refuses.
